<thought>Based on the 13C NMR data, the low‑field signals (≈10–35 ppm) correspond to aliphatic carbons. The peaks at 34.53 ppm appear twice (two equivalent carbons), and there are additional distinct peaks at 22.80, 21.35, and 19.20 ppm. All of these chemical shifts fall within the typical range for methyl (CH₃) carbons. Counting each carbon signal in this region, including the two equivalent ones, gives a total of **5** methyl carbons.</thought>
<final_answer>5</final_answer>
